help.doing: What chat as a whole is doing in this window; pick every reaction a clear share of the lines shows (at least one).
help.aimed_at: Who or what most of the reaction is about; pick one.
help.feeling: How chat feels about what it is reacting to; pick one.
help.tone: How chat says it; optional, and leaving it blank means no clear tone.
help.not_sure: Instead of answering a question, mark it not sure with one or more reasons; a not-sure answer carries no value.
help.spread: How the reaction moves through chat; counted from the window, shown to help, never labeled.
help.cause: Optional note on what caused the reaction, filled only from evidence outside chat; empty by default.
help.doing.laughing: Chat finds something funny: laughter words, laughing emotes, joke replies.
help.doing.cheering: Chat celebrates or hypes a success: "lets go", "gg", clapping or hype emotes.
help.doing.shocked: Chat reacts to something sudden or surprising: "what", "no way", "omg".
help.doing.tense: Chat is on edge about what happens next: "oh no", "careful", waiting for a result.
help.doing.sad: Chat shows sadness, sympathy or disappointment: "rip", "nooo", crying emotes.
help.doing.asking: Chat asks questions about what is happening, the stream or the game.
help.doing.advising: Chat tells the streamer what to do: tips, instructions, backseating.
help.doing.complaining: Chat complains or vents frustration about the stream, the game, the tech or anything else.
help.doing.chatting_as_usual: Ordinary chat with no shared reaction: greetings, side talk, unrelated lines.
help.doing.other: A clear shared reaction that none of the other values describes.
help.aimed_at.streamer: The streamer: what they did, said or decided.
help.aimed_at.game_content: The game or content on screen: an event, a character, a play, a scene.
help.aimed_at.guest: A guest, co-streamer or other person on stream who is not the streamer.
help.aimed_at.chat_itself: Chat itself: other chatters, a running chat joke, a chant, chat's own behaviour.
help.aimed_at.tech_problem: A technical problem: lag, a dropped stream, broken audio or video.
help.aimed_at.unclear: No single target stands out: the lines point at different things or at nothing in particular.
help.feeling.supportive: Chat is on the target's side: praise, encouragement, sympathy, hype.
help.feeling.critical: Chat is against the target: criticism, mockery, blame, frustration.
help.feeling.mixed: Chat is split: clear support and clear criticism in the same window.
help.feeling.neutral: No clear stance for or against: ordinary chatter, plain questions, plain facts.
help.tone.playful: Joking, teasing or light-hearted, even when the words sound harsh.
help.tone.serious: Earnest and literal: real concern, real advice, plain statements.
help.tone.sarcastic: Says the opposite of what it means, usually to mock or tease.
help.tone.hostile: Aggressive or abusive toward someone, past playful teasing.
help.tone.no_clear_tone: No tone stands out; a real answer, not missing data.
help.not_sure.unclear: The lines don't let you answer: too few, too vague, or the context is off screen.
help.not_sure.conflicting: The lines point to different answers and none clearly wins.
help.not_sure.cause_missing: The answer depends on what happened on stream, and chat alone doesn't show it.
help.not_sure.unknown_in_joke: Chat is running a joke, meme or reference you don't know.
help.not_sure.needs_review: A contested reading, such as a contested emote ID, that needs a careful second look; never guess.
help.spread.repeated_emotes: Many lines repeat the same emote.
help.spread.chant: Many lines repeat the same word or phrase.
help.spread.back_and_forth: Chatters reply to each other in a conversation.
help.spread.separate_messages: Many posters write their own lines with no shared pattern.
help.spread.few_posters: Too few distinct posters to call it a chat-wide reaction.
help.cause_source.clip: The cause note comes from watching the clip.
help.cause_source.game: The cause note comes from the game's own state or events.
help.cause_source.stream_title: The cause note comes from the stream title.
